implementation_notes: The pattern text's own C++ realization is written by hand: the subject answers a shared Extension* for an identifier - a string guarded by a registry, or better a typeid/type_index - and the client narrows it with dynamic_cast, treating nullptr as 'this component does not support the interface' (the pattern text does exactly this before calling FirstWord/NextWord). dynamic_cast needs RTTI and a polymorphic hierarchy, is hierarchy-based rather than structural, and quietly loses the query in builds configured without RTTI, while nothing in the standard library supplies the extension storage or the registry. Use this form for the canonical structure; prefer the Qt variant when its object model is already in the stack (COM's IUnknown::QueryInterface is the same idea in the Windows ecosystem), and the C++17 variant when you want the extension base class to disappear.
pitfalls: dynamic_cast returns nullptr both for 'unsupported' and for a build without RTTI; the query silently disappears on -fno-rtti configurations.
The returned Extension* points at an object the subject owns: returning a fresh adapter per call leaks or costs an allocation per query - cache it per subject.
typeid keys are unique only within one binary, so extension ids crossing shared-library boundaries must use the type_index of a shared interface, not a locally declared typeid.
dynamic_cast on a reference throws std::bad_cast; only the pointer form satisfies the total-query rule.

variants.name: Type-indexed std::any storage (modern C++)
variants.implementation_notes: C++17 lets the subject store extensions in a type-indexed heterogeneous map and answer a template query: look the entry up by std::type_index and return std::any_cast<T>(&any), which is nullptr on a type mismatch, so the query stays total and the Extension base class disappears. Trade-offs: std::any requires CopyConstructible values (store std::shared_ptr for stateful or non-copyable extensions) and typically allocates per stored extension, and type identity is again binary-scoped.
pitfalls: std::any_cast<T>(&a) returns nullptr on mismatch but std::any_cast<T>(a) throws std::bad_any_cast - use the pointer form for a total query.
std::any requires CopyConstructible: hold std::shared_ptr<T> or std::reference_wrapper for non-copyable extensions.

variants.name: Qt interface query via qobject_cast
variants.implementation_notes: Inside a Qt codebase the query already exists: give the extension interface a unique IID with Q_DECLARE_INTERFACE, register it on the implementing class with Q_INTERFACES, and ask with qobject_cast<Interface*>(obj), which uses the meta-object system instead of RTTI and therefore works across dynamic-library boundaries. The base interface (QObject) is untouched, the extension interface is a pure-virtual class, and a null cast result is the total answer - but the mechanism applies only to QObject-derived subjects and needs moc-generated metadata.
pitfalls: Q_INTERFACES must list every interface the class implements, and Q_DECLARE_INTERFACE must sit outside any namespace or casts fail at run time.
qobject_cast needs generated meta-object data (moc) and a QObject-derived subject; the interface itself must be a pure-virtual class with a virtual destructor.
The IID is a string contract: changing it silently breaks casts across libraries that were compiled against the old value.
